newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds inch higher, agencies buy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds inch higher, agencies buy.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities crept higher by late Wednesday afternoon, while yield spreads widened moderately to Treasuries.
To narrow the yield spreads between Treasuries and mortgage-backeds, the agencies stepped in and bought back premium coupons, said a Midwest trader, adding that "that is an ongoing program."
Nevertheless, the market was relatively quiet with the typical "ebbs and flows," he said.
Late on Wednesday, pass-throughs were up 6/32 to 11/32 in coupons of 7.0 percent or smaller, and were up 2/32 to 5/32 in premium coupons.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 12/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 7/32 at 99-11/32, yielding 109 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable FNMAs were up 6/32 at 99-12/32, and FHLMCs were up 6/32 to 99-18/32.
